AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To evaluate the effects of surgery and a postoperative progressive home exercise program on gait parameters among individuals operated with total knee arthroplasty.

AbstractText.Label: SUBJECTS
AbstractText.content: 108 patients (84 females, 24 males, mean age 69 years).

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTIONS
AbstractText.content: Patients were equally randomized into an exercise group (EG) and control group (CG). The 12-months progressive home exercise program starting two months postoperatively was compared to usual care.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Gait analysis was performed using the Gaitrite electronic walkway system. In addition, knee extension and flexion strength were measured by a dynamometer preoperatively, and pain on visual analog scale (VAS) at two months and 14 months postoperatively.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: At the 12-month follow-up, maximal gait velocity (p=0.006), cadence (p=0.003) and stance time (p=0.039) showed a greater increase among EG than CG. All the other gait parameters improved among both groups, but with not statistically discernible difference between groups. Weak correlations were found between changes in maximal gait velocity and the knee extension (r=-0.31, p=0.002), flexion strength (r=0.28, p=0.004) and pain during loading (r=-0.27, p=0.005) values.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: The intervention produced statistically significant changes in maximal gait velocity, cadence and stance times in the exercise group compared to controls. Although the average change was small it is of importance that biggest changes occurred in those with low performance.
